record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: For polygonal symplectic billiards, classify all polygons with the property that every symplectic billiard orbit is periodic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Polygonal symplectic billiards are defined as follows. Let P be a convex polygon in the affine plane R^2 equipped with the standard symplectic (area) form ω(u,v) = det(u,v). For an ordered pair of points (x, y) with x, y on the boundary ∂P (and x, y in the interiors of edges of P), the symplectic billiard map T sends (x, y) to (y, z), where z ∈ ∂P is the unique point such that the chord [x, z] is parallel to the edge of P containing y. An orbit is the sequence {(x_n, x_{n+1})} obtained by iterating T, and it is called periodic if there exists N ≥ 1 with x_{n+N} = x_n for all n.

Problem: Classify all convex polygons P ⊂ R^2 with the property that every symplectic billiard orbit on P is periodic.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification appears to remain open. Known sufficient classes include affine-regular polygons and trapezoids, for which all symplectic billiard orbits are periodic with explicit periods (Albers–Banhatti–Sadlo–Schwartz–Tabachnikov, "Polygonal symplectic billiards", arXiv:1912.09404). No complete classification of polygons with entirely periodic dynamics has been reported in subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: Polygonal symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: If a polygon is affine-regular or is a trapezoid, then all orbits are periodic, with explicitly described periods.
status_evidence.claim: Affine-regular polygons and trapezoids are known examples where every symplectic billiard orbit is periodic, but the full classification is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Outer length billiards on polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on polygonal billiards variants continues to investigate periodicity questions.
status_evidence.claim: The literature continues to investigate periodicity in polygonal billiards variants, indicating the classification question remains active.
